findings.title: Three of the four cross-class-mutations cells state the expectation of a different named negative test than the one they implement.
findings.measurement: occupancy v2 namedCorpusClasses[1].passProperty carries four distinct sentences, one per named negative test, in the same order the class's exactByteIntent names the tests: (1) "A writer of one included class cannot commit into the other included class's store." for cross-class writes; (2) "Neither included class becomes Authoritative evidence by copy, rename, or citation." for cache-to-authority promotion; (3) "An undeclared Plan input fails." for undeclared Plan inputs; (4) "A component evidence commit fails." for component evidence commits. g19-input-corpus.v2 carries the matching one-to-one split in initialStates[*].stateNamed: `cross-class writes`, `cache-to-authority promotion`, `undeclared Plan inputs`, `component evidence commits`. The subject gives all four members the identical expected string "Named negative-test cell present. A writer of one included class cannot commit into the other included class's store. Qualification remains unexecuted." — sentence (1) only. For G19.mutations.cache-to-authority-promotion, G19.mutations.undeclared-plan-inputs and G19.mutations.component-evidence-commits the stated expectation is a property those cells do not test, and the property they do test is stated nowhere in the catalog. Measured: 2 distinct expected strings across 12 members; 3 of the 4 mutation cells mis-stated.
findings.whyNotAdvisory: expected is the catalog's per-cell statement of what the cell expects. The four mutation cells are not four copies of one test; they are file 04's four separately named negative tests, which is why g19-input-corpus.v2 named them separately and why occupancy v2 gives each its own pass sentence. As authored, three cells carry an oracle that does not correspond to them, so the catalog does not yet implement the leftover-design it claims for those three named tests.
findings.internalAsymmetry: The eight class-lifecycle-matrix members do not have this problem, and they avoid it by a different technique: each cites the property by path ("fails occupancy v2 namedCorpusClasses[0].passProperty") rather than quoting one sentence out of it. The four mutation members neither cite namedCorpusClasses[1].passProperty by path nor quote the sentence matching their own cell. The safe pattern is already present in the same artifact and in the D-298-accepted g20-fixture-corpus.v5, whose uniform expected strings reference the passProperty by path and quote no single sentence from it.
findings.precedent: g23-fixture-corpus.v4 and g21-fixture-corpus.v1 — the two accepted first-authoring corpora whose members are named negative tests rather than matrix cells — give every member a distinct per-cell expected (4 of 4 and 2 of 2 distinct). This subject's matrix half follows the g20 path-reference pattern and its negative-test half follows neither.
findings.ifEverRepaired: Either give each of the four mutation members the passProperty sentence matching its own named negative test, or replace the quoted sentence with the same path reference the matrix members use (occupancy v2 namedCorpusClasses[1].passProperty). Either repair is confined to three expected strings in the subject; it touches no fixture file, so the twelve fixture digests and the whole recordedInputs block are unaffected, and the subject's own digest is the only one that moves.
findings.blocking: Blocks ACCEPT under the stated decision rule. Does not block the authoring warrant, the platform quotation, the fixture construction, or the id binding, all of which measured clean.
